historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management medium-term outlook (~5% adjusted EBITDA growth post-2026), faded; not equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.3-0.9%) diverges far more than 30% from revenue and EPS CAGRs and is not usable: dividends have exceeded GAAP earnings, and book equity moves with FX translation and share issuance for acquisitions. Revenue CAGR is commodity pass-through and EPS CAGR is distorted by derivative marks (FY2022 trough).
historical_growth.notes: FCF series is OCF less capital expenditures less equity-settled SBC (C$28-113m); interest income is not stripped because there is no net cash. Owner FCF fell from C$6.5bn (FY2022) to C$3.2bn (FY2025) because capex roughly doubled (C$4.6bn to C$9.0bn) while OCF was flat at C$12-14bn: the decline is the growth program, not operating deterioration. Reported EBITDA (company basis) grew from C$14.2bn (FY2021) to C$20.5bn (FY2025), about 9.5% a year, mostly through the US$14bn gas-utility acquisitions funded with debt and ~150m new shares.

scenario_narratives.base: Enbridge delivers what it has guided: C$20.5bn of adjusted EBITDA in 2026, about 5% a year through 2030 as the C$39bn secured backlog (BC Pipeline expansions, Woodfibre LNG, Gulf Coast storage, Mainline optimisation, utility rate-base programs) enters service, plus the Tallgrass and Salt Creek crude tuck-ins in 2027. Each dollar of growth capital earns roughly an 11% EBITDA yield, close to the cost of capital once tax and sustaining spend are counted, so growth adds little value beyond what it costs. After 2030 the program shrinks, capex falls from ~60% of EBITDA to ~26%, and the business becomes what its tolls and rate bases already describe: a 2% inflation-linked annuity capitalised at 18x free cash flow, about 12x EBITDA, in line with where large North American midstream trades today.
scenario_narratives.bull: Gas demand from data centres, coal-to-gas switching and LNG exports keeps the backlog full past 2033 at brownfield returns, so EBITDA compounds at 5-6% for most of the decade. The Mainline Tolling Settlement is renewed in 2028 inside the current 11-14.5% return collar with the system still full at ~3.1 mmbpd, the US gas utilities earn their allowed ROEs after the Ohio and North Carolina cases, and leverage drifts down from ~5x without new equity. Cash taxes plateau as guided. The market pays 20x terminal free cash flow (about 13x EBITDA) for a larger, more gas-weighted and more regulated mix.
scenario_narratives.bear: The risk is not volume collapse but the terms on which a 46%-levered asset base is re-priced. The 2028 Mainline negotiation settles lower as shippers gain alternatives (Trans Mountain expansion headroom, weaker Western Canadian supply growth) and Line 5 litigation adds cost; state commissions repeat the 2025 Ohio disallowance; projects run over budget under steel tariffs; and refinancing C$7-8bn of maturities a year at higher spreads pushes management to issue equity again to hold the ~5x debt/EBITDA ceiling. EBITDA still grows, at 1.5-3%, but the capital to get there is no smaller, sustaining capex stays above depreciation recovery, and the exit multiple falls to about 10x EBITDA, the level of the 2020 trough. Because C$125bn of claims rank ahead of the common, an enterprise value about a quarter lower removes roughly half of the equity.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Enbridge is valued as a leveraged toll road: an unlevered free cash flow stream after ALL investment (growth capital included, faded as the disclosed backlog completes), discounted at a 6.75% CAD cost of capital, less every claim ranking ahead of the common shares. The company's own 'distributable cash flow' is not used as the flow because it excludes growth capital that the same management needs to produce the growth it guides to. Because debt, preferred and NCI are about 46% of enterprise value, equity value is roughly twice as sensitive to the discount rate and exit multiple as enterprise value; the sensitivity grid matters more here than the point estimate. A 15% required return is not available from this asset at anything near the market price: the stock is a 5.7% yield growing 3-5%.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount-rate sensitivity: +/-1pp of WACC moves base value per share by about 16% with the 18x terminal cap binding; without the cap (Gordon at 6.75%/2.0% is ~21x) the swing would be far larger
Terminal assumptions carry most of the value: 18x terminal FCF (~12x EBITDA) and sustaining capex below depreciation are judgments, not disclosures
FY2025 adjusted EBITDA (C$19.8bn) is estimated from the 10-K, not read from the earnings release; a C$0.2bn error is about C$1/share
Mainline Tolling Settlement expiry in 2028 and US gas-utility rate cases
USD/CAD: more than half of EBITDA and much of the debt is USD; the USD value depends on the 0.7008 rate, which refresh_price does not update
Further common equity issuance to defend the credit rating would dilute a share count the model holds flat
Risk-free rates in wacc_rationale are assumed, not fetched

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (NYSE: ENB) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 45.03-58.45 USD. TSX parity and CADUSD=X from the same API.
data_sources.financials: Q3-2026 10-Q (balance sheet 30-Sep-2026, cash flow, share count, acquisitions); FY2025 10-K (cash flow, SBC, capital program); ENB_Metrics.csv and kpis (ReportedEBITDA, segment EBITDA, cash_taxes).
data_sources.qualitative: ENB_Analysis.json (2026-11-15): FY2026 guidance, medium-term ~5% outlook, backlog, risks.

inputs.share_count_basis: 2,228.9m common shares outstanding at 30-Oct-2026 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover, after the 44.7m-share September 2026 offering) plus 6m dilutive options/RSUs (Q3-2026 EPS note). Held flat: SBC is expensed in the flows and the base case assumes the secured program is equity self-funded, as management states. A further equity raise would be genuine non-SBC dilution and is a bear-case risk not modelled in the count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K statement of changes in equity, equity-settled stock-based compensation C$113m (ENB_Annual_FY2025.txt:9983). The C$285m in core_metrics is total plan expense including cash-settled units, which are already a cash cost inside EBITDA. Enbridge's adjusted EBITDA does not add SBC back, so the margin path is grossed up by 0.173% of revenue and the same amount deducted on the SBC line: SBC stays visible and is charged once.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in CAD; NYSE quote in USD. CAD->USD 0.7008 (Yahoo CADUSD=X, 2026-11-14). Parity check against the TSX listing: ENB.TO C$67.96 x 0.7008 = US$47.63 vs the NYSE close of US$47.67 (0.1% tie), which confirms rate, direction and a 1:1 share basis. Roughly 55-60% of EBITDA is USD-denominated, so the CAD value itself moves with USD/CAD; the guidance assumes 1.37.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 6.75%, built in CAD with a USD tilt to match the flows. Cost of equity 8.0% = blended risk-free ~3.8% (assumed ~3.3% Canada 10-year and ~4.2% US 10-year, weighted to the ~55-60% USD EBITDA; not re-fetched, check against live yields) + beta 0.85 x 5.0% ERP. Cost of debt 5.1% PRE-tax (FY2026 run-rate interest ~C$4.9bn on ~C$110bn is 4.5% embedded; marginal issuance ~5.2%; preference shares and hybrids ~6%). Market weights ~54% equity / 46% debt, preferred and NCI. The debt cost is deliberately pre-tax because the cash tax path in the flows is the actual LEVERED cash tax (interest shield already inside it); using an after-tax debt cost as well would count the shield twice. One WACC for all three scenarios: risk is charged in the flows and the weights, not the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Immaterial (interest on lease liabilities C$29m in FY2025). US GAAP operating leases are already expensed inside EBITDA; lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. No separate lease line.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated EBITDA. Noncontrolling interests (C$2,701m) and redeemable NCI (C$1,433m, KKR/Apollo Westcoast and First Nations partnerships) are deducted once in the equity bridge at book, which is ~11-12x the ~C$360m/yr of NCI distributions. Preference shares (C$6,818m) are deducted at book. Equity-investee income sits inside EBITDA, so the C$22.5bn of long-term investments is NOT added to the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: unlevered owner-FCF component DCF (operating-company row of dcf-methods plus the non-US adaptations: dual currency, NCI, preferred). Chosen over the FCFE-at-cost-of-equity route used for SO because Enbridge's operating cash flow covers maintenance and a large share of growth capital, the capital program is finite and disclosed (C$39bn secured through 2033) so capex can be faded explicitly, and the claims ahead of common equity (debt, hybrids, preferred, NCI) are too large and too varied to bury inside a cost of equity. Cross-check on the equity route: C$3.88 dividend growing 3% at an 8.0% cost of equity is about C$80; at 9% about C$67. REVENUE IS A SCALING INDEX, NOT A FORECAST: reported revenue is ~53% commodity marketing pass-through (FY2025 C$65.2bn; 9M-2026 already C$72.8bn) and carries no information about earnings. base_revenue is FY2025 reported revenue, the EBITDA margin is held flat at 30.54%, and growth_rates are therefore ADJUSTED EBITDA growth. FY0 adjusted EBITDA is taken as ~C$19.8bn: reported FY2025 EBITDA of C$20,477m less the C$1,334m unrealised derivative gain plus C$570m impairment, consistent with the 2025 guidance range of C$19.4-20.0bn; the exact adjusted figure is in the earnings release, not the 10-K, and is an estimate here. Year 1 (FY2026) ties to the guidance midpoint of C$20.5bn, which management said it is tracking to. CAPEX is total cash investment: capital expenditures plus long-term investment contributions and intangibles, net of equity-investee distributions in excess of earnings (FY2025 ~C$10.8bn; 9M-2026 C$9.6bn, so FY2026 ~C$12.5bn). ACQUISITIONS: Salt Creek (C$892m, closed 9-Oct-2026) and Tallgrass crude (C$3,620m, expected Q4-2026) are after the balance-sheet date; their cost is deducted in the equity bridge and their EBITDA (~C$0.45bn) is the extra ~2pp in year-2 growth. The C$4.9bn of cash at 30-Sep includes the September equity proceeds earmarked for them. last_fcf/reported_fcf are levered (after-interest) OCF less capex and are retained for audit only; the forward build is unlevered. Buybacks: none since FY2023; the flat share count is a modelling convention, not funded repurchase. The 15% hurdle entry price is far below intrinsic value: that is the arithmetic of demanding 15% from a 46%-levered asset discounted at 6.75%, not an error.

bear.rationale: Bottom of guidance, then the same capital buys roughly half the EBITDA growth: cost overruns, a less favourable Mainline settlement after 2028, utility ROE cuts. Sustaining capex stays at 30% of EBITDA (above D&A recovery) and cash tax rises faster.

base.rationale: Growth is adjusted EBITDA growth: FY2026 guidance midpoint C$20.5bn (+3.5%), FY2027 5% organic plus ~2pp from Tallgrass/Salt Creek, then management's ~5% through 2030 fading to 2.5% as the secured backlog (through 2033) runs off. Capex is total investment at 61% of EBITDA in FY2026 (~C$12.5bn) fading to 26% (~C$7.7bn in year-10 money, about 0.9x D&A). D&A 28.5% of EBITDA. Cash tax is the levered cash rate on EBIT, 8.5% in FY2025 (C$1.2bn), rising to 16% as accelerated-depreciation deferral unwinds; management says cash taxes plateau late in the decade.

bull.rationale: Top of guidance in FY2026, backlog replenished at 6-7x build multiples by gas-power and LNG demand, Mainline re-contracted on equal or better terms; terminal capex 23% of EBITDA.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default: debt/EBITDA sits at the top of management's range (~5x), a single settlement (Mainline, expiring 2028) governs close to a third of EBITDA, and equity was issued in September 2026, which shows the self-funding model is already tight. Base 50%: guidance has been met for many consecutive years and ~98% of EBITDA is contracted or regulated. Bull cut to 25% from 35%: it needs backlog replenishment, a clean Mainline renewal and a higher exit multiple together, and the 2% terminal growth already credits inflation pass-through.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
